structure.overview: Ms. Luttrell, the applicant, sought judicial review of a decision refusing her Temporary Resident Permit (TRP) application, arguing errors in the immigration officer's assessment. The respondent, the Minister of Citizenship and Immigration, contended the review was moot due to Ms. Luttrell's subsequent grant of a one-year TRP. The Federal Court agreed the matter was moot and dismissed the judicial review application without addressing the merits.

sections.label: Court's analysis on mootness and judicial economy

summaries.speaker: party
summaries.summary: Ms. Luttrell argues the Officer erred by applying the wrong standard, misassessing her immigration history, and misjudging the child's best interest.
idea_list: Error in best interest of child assessment

summaries.speaker: party
summaries.summary: The Minister contends the judicial review is moot because Ms. Luttrell was granted a one-year TRP in December 2024.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The Court agrees the review is moot due to the valid TRP and declines to consider the matter on its merits.

summaries.speaker: below
summaries.summary: Ms. Luttrell's 2021 permanent residence application on humanitarian grounds was refused, and judicial review was dismissed the same year.

summaries.speaker: party
summaries.summary: Ms. Luttrell applied for a TRP in February 2022 citing no criminal record, family ties, work with disabled children, and community advocacy.

summaries.speaker: below
summaries.summary: On August 31, 2023, the Officer upheld the TRP refusal, citing lack of exceptional circumstances and Ms. Luttrell's ability to regularize status otherwise.

summaries.speaker: party
summaries.summary: Ms. Luttrell applied for an open work permit on January 23, 2025, which remains under processing.

summaries.speaker: party
summaries.summary: Ms. Luttrell argues the review is not moot due to future TRP needs and urges the Court to exercise discretion to hear the matter.
idea_list: Future TRP need keeps controversy alive
Collateral consequences and judicial economy arguments

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The Court is unconvinced by Ms. Luttrell's arguments that the matter is not moot.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The Court agrees the case is moot as Ms. Luttrell holds a valid TRP, so judicial review would have no practical effect.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The Court finds Ms. Luttrell's possible future TRP need speculative and insufficient to maintain a live controversy.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The Court finds no adversarial context as Ms. Luttrell already has a TRP and the Minister's arguments lack vigour.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The Court rejects collateral consequences argument, noting TRP decisions are discretionary and prior decisions don't bind officers.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Judicial economy favors dismissal since the case has no practical effect and existing cases address TRP standards.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Judicial resources already spent make judicial economy a neutral factor in deciding to hear the case.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The Court notes no question of general importance arises and Ms. Luttrell made no submissions on this factor, weighing against hearing the case.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The Court concludes the Borowski test and interests of justice favor dismissing Ms. Luttrell's judicial review application.

summaries.speaker: other
summaries.summary: The parties did not propose any question of general importance for certification.
